skills.notes: App-gold ships no plugin manifest. Claude Code discovers project-level skills directly from .claude/skills/ with no manifest required — this is the documented project-skills path, distinct from the plugin-install path used by plugin-gold repos. Validation checks that path directly instead of `claude plugin validate .`, which requires a .claude-plugin/plugin.json this repo shape does not ship.

subagents.notes: Claude Code's documented project-level subagent path is .claude/agents/*.md, discovered with no plugin manifest required — the same non-plugin convention as .claude/skills/, not the root agents/ directory this repo's own .claude-plugin/plugin.json points `agents` at (that field exists only for the plugin-install route, which app-gold does not use). `claude plugin validate .` is dropped because it requires a .claude-plugin/plugin.json this repo shape does not and should not ship.

parallel_subagents.notes: Multiple Agent calls in one message run concurrently. This is a Claude Code session behaviour, not something this repo's shape gates, so validation only proves the CLI is present rather than requiring a plugin manifest that has nothing to do with the claim.

subagents.notes: Demoted from 'native' 2026-09-08. The claim rested on two things, and neither survived checking. (1) The note cited platform-targets.json — but that file's per-target `capabilities` array is a DERIVED mirror of THIS registry (scripts/check-platform-targets.sh says so in its header), so the row was citing itself. (2) The validation was `jq empty .codex-plugin/plugin.json`, which passes on any valid JSON. Against the upstream manifest spec, .codex-plugin/plugin.json defines name, version, description, author, homepage, repository, license, keywords, skills, hooks, mcpServers, apps and interface — there is no agents or subagents field, and no documented folder discovery of an agents/ directory. This repo also ships no Codex agent mirror, unlike .gemini/agents/, which exists precisely because Gemini needed one. Codex CLI does have a subagents feature, and it is deliberately outside the plugin system: subagents are standalone .toml files in $CODEX_HOME/agents/ or a per-repo .codex/agents/, and bundling one inside a plugin manifest is an OPEN feature request (https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/28491, closed as a duplicate of #18988). So the missing field is not an oversight in the spec — there is no plugin-packaging path to this capability at all today. The status stays 'unknown' rather than 'unsupported' because the capability exists on the surface; what is unestablished is a route from this plugin to it, and 'unsupported' would claim Codex lacks subagents, which is false. The identical 'Cloud subagents can run on their own VMs (2026-08-19)' sentence also sat on the cursor row verbatim, date included — one note copied, not two facts established.
subagents.fallback: Run the role inline in the main session, sequentially, with a narrowed scope.

skills.notes: Measured on 0.55.1: Gemini discovers skills exactly one level below a skills root, so the canonical two-level skills/<domain>/<name>/ tree resolves to ZERO skills. scripts/build-gemini-extension.sh generates a flat symlink mirror at .gemini/skills/ (one symlink per skill, so still exactly one copy in the repo), which Gemini then reads natively — in-workspace with no install at all, or via a single gemini skills install --path .gemini/skills. This row is about the generated mirror, not the canonical tree. NOTE: Gemini follows symlinks for skill discovery; OpenCode does not, at any level. Do not port one platform's mirror strategy to the other.
skills.fallback: None needed — the mirror is committed, and scripts/check-gemini-adapter.sh fails rather than shipping an adapter that finds nothing. Regenerate with make gemini-extension; never hand-edit .gemini/skills/. One live failure mode: an untrusted workspace folder silently skips the mirror, and the only clue is Gemini logging 'Skipping project agents due to untrusted folder'.

skill_auto_invocation.notes: Gemini follows the Agent Skills model, but its selection behaviour has not been measured.

subagents.notes: The CANONICAL form does not load: agents/*.md are read from the extension root and rejected with 'tools.0: Invalid tool name', because Gemini wants tools as an array of its own tool names while this repo's agents declare Claude's (Read, Grep, Glob, Bash) as a string. A GENERATED form does: scripts/build-gemini-extension.sh emits .gemini/agents/*.md with tools as a YAML array of real Gemini names (read_file, search_file_content, glob, run_shell_command), verified against the loader rather than guessed, and omits model: entirely — a Claude alias like 'sonnet' passes validation and then fails at invocation. Verified on 0.55.1: all agents load with no errors.
subagents.fallback: Regenerate with make gemini-extension; never hand-edit .gemini/agents/. Installing the extension still emits a harmless load error for the canonical agents/ at the extension root — noisy, not fatal, and unfixable from this side (no subdirectory flag, no manifest field relocates it).

hooks.notes: This adapter ships no hooks, by design — a statement about the adapter, not a verdict on Gemini. Measured on 0.55.1, read from the shipped bundle rather than the docs: Gemini accepts the outer {"hooks": {...}} shape of the Claude Code schema without complaint, AND accepts an invented event name just as silently, so loading proves nothing about firing. The vocabularies partially overlap rather than differ wholesale — of this repo's ten declared events, three (SessionStart, SessionEnd, Notification) are real Gemini events, four (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop) exist only as keys in the gemini hooks migrate --from-claude mapping table, and three (DirectoryAdded, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove) have no counterpart at all. Whether the three shared events actually fire was NOT verified, so no claim is made in either direction. Not 'unsupported' — that would assert a measured failure that was never measured, and would also imply the dropped-in Claude file is wholly inert when three of its handlers name events Gemini has.
hooks.fallback: Guards become explicit in-skill steps plus CI checks. gemini hooks migrate --from-claude can translate them into personal settings.
